transcript:
This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros
to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Ryland Barton. President Trump campaigned in South Carolina
today as he encourages Republicans to show up for Darlene Graham in a critical Senate contest.
If you want to keep this growth going, you must vote Republican and you must
vote for really an amazing person, Darlene Graham.
Graham was appointed to fill the seat held by her brother, the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham,
after his death. She's trying to fend off a challenge from pediatrician Annie Andrews
in a state that hasn't sent a Democrat to the Senate in nearly three decades.
Earlier in the day, Trump cast doubt on whether Alaska Democratic Senate candidate
Mary Peltola would be seated if she wins after a New York Times story accusing her
campaign of recruiting a candidate with the same name as her Republican opponent
incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan. When you look at that, nobody knows what to press.
We've done studies. Nobody knows. They have no idea who the Dan Sullivan is.
NPR has not independently confirmed the New York Times' reporting. Alaska Republican
Governor Mike Dunleavy ordered an investigation. Tens of millions of people have already voted
early. NPR's Stephen Fowler reports black voter turnout continues to be higher than it generally
has been in previous midterms. In states like Louisiana, South Carolina, and Georgia, which
have a large share of black voters, there's a notable increase in black voter turnout so far.
Some of that is driven by the Supreme Court decision earlier this year and a case out of
Louisiana that curbed part of the Voting Rights Act, which led to many Republican-led states
redrawing congressional maps to eliminate districts that favor Democrats. The higher
turnout, combined with higher-than-usual disapproval ratings among Republican voters,
has the potential to make several races closer than expected. Which is one reason why President
Trump is packing these final days with campaign stops and virtual appearances in those states
where he won in 2024. Stephen Fowler, NPR News, Atlanta. Shares and the chip maker Intel have
tanked today after the company said the personal computer market is weak and will continue to be
deep into next year. As NPR's John Roach reports, the company says it faces supply chain problems.
Intel's share price slumped by more than 21 percent in after-hours trading after it
reported its quarterly earnings. The company's revenue in the latest quarter actually beat
expectations. But the chip maker reported headwinds in meeting AI-driven demand,
and it said its biggest driver of revenue, the PC market, was soft.
CEO Lip Bhutan said there was a PC market correction that's accelerating because of
memory chip shortages and limited IT budgets. He said current conditions are expected to
exist until the memory crunch caused by huge investments in AI data centers returns to normal.
John Roach, NPR News. A historic drop for Google parent company Alphabet's stock dragged the U.S.
stock market lower today. The S&P 500 fell more than a quarter percent, even though the
wide majority of stocks rose within the index and across Wall Street. This is NPR News from Washington.
The Federal Trade Commission is ordering Delta Airlines, Walmart and other companies to provide
detailed information on how they use consumers' data when they're setting prices.
It comes as customers are increasingly concerned about pricing technology
and the use of artificial intelligence to collect and interpret vast amounts of data.
Halloween is just around the corner, and candy prices may have you scared stiff,
as NPR's Joe Hernandez reports that the cost of chocolate and other sweets is rising.
According to the latest federal data, prices for candy and gum are up 7.7 percent in one year and
more than 18 percent in two years. One major culprit is chocolate. After drought and heavy
rains in places like West Africa hurt cocoa harvests in recent seasons. Global cocoa production
is rebounding, but consumer chocolate prices remain elevated, and shoppers are pulling back.
That's according to data from Circana, which tracks sales in supermarkets across the U.S.
They found that people have been buying less chocolate each year for several years running,
but dollar sales are up, which means people are spending more money on chocolate but getting
less of it. Joe Hernandez, NPR News. The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime reports a sharp
rise in poppy cultivation and opium production in Afghanistan over the past year. It marks the
first significant increase since the Taliban imposed a narcotics ban in 2022. The agency
attributes the rise to deepening poverty, pushing farmers to cultivate opium clandestinely.
Afghanistan was the world's biggest opium producer. When the Taliban seized power in 2021, the U.N.
agency called for international support to help farmers find alternatives to the illicit crop.
It's NPR. This message comes from IXL, a learning platform for helping kids build confidence
and get up to speed fast. One subscription covers math, science, and reading for all
children in a household. Receive 20 percent off at IXL.com/NPR.
